hypothesis: A 12-call stop only when at least four distinct receipt-delivered wide source ranges exist, otherwise continuing to at most 24 discovery calls, improves final source selection and materially reduces tokens and time against native convergence across new Rust and Go tasks.
decision_rule: Run and report both tasks regardless of the first result. Seal predictions before pinned native scoring. On each task candidate Span-F1 and File-F1 must strictly exceed control, with strictly lower known model tokens and measured duration. Both tasks must pass all four gates for a replicated claim. Unscored is inconclusive, never a win. A later source change requires a new cohort.
gold_posture: Only source-only task statements and pinned repository availability were inspected; neither exact task had an instance ID in prior benchmark evidence, and exact gold was not inspected before freeze.
claim_ceiling: Two-task adaptive G01 replication, not a full ContextBench campaign or complete cross-benchmark ARE proof.
open_questions: Does the adaptive rule avoid sparse-read accuracy failure on a new Rust task?
Does it preserve large token and time savings on a new Go task?
